definitions.explanation: Sake that has been warmed, typically to around 50°C. Traditionally served in a small ceramic flask ({徳利|とっくり}) with matching small cups (お{猪口|ちょこ}).

examples.japanese: {寒|さむ}い{夜|よる}は{熱燗|あつかん}がいい。
examples.english: Hot sake is great on a cold night.

examples.japanese: {熱燗|あつかん}を{一本|いっぽん}つけてください。
examples.english: Please warm up one flask of sake.

examples.japanese: {居酒屋|いざかや}で{熱燗|あつかん}を{飲|の}みながら{鍋|なべ}を{囲|かこ}むのが{冬|ふゆ}の{楽|たの}しみだ。
examples.english: Sharing a hot pot while drinking warm sake at an izakaya is one of winter's pleasures.

notes:
Compound of {熱|あつ} (hot) + {燗|かん} (warmed sake). The verb for warming sake is {燗|かん}をつける or simply つける.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {熱燗|あつかん}をつける: to warm up sake
- {熱燗|あつかん}{一本|いっぽん}: one flask of hot sake
- {熱燗|あつかん}を{飲|の}む: to drink hot sake

TEMPERATURE LEVELS:
Sake has several traditional serving temperatures, each with its own name:
- {日向燗|ひなたかん}: ~30°C (lukewarm)
- ぬる{燗|かん}: ~40°C (warm)
- {上燗|じょうかん}: ~45°C (warmer)
- {熱燗|あつかん}: ~50°C (hot)
- とびきり{燗|かん}: ~55°C+ (very hot)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {冷酒|れいしゅ}: cold sake
- {常温|じょうおん}: room-temperature sake
